name: Adolf Hitler
role: Leader of the Nazi Party; dictator of Germany (1933-1945)
summary: Leader of the Nazi Party, who held that history is a struggle between races, saw Germans as a racial community entitled to living space in the East, and was hostile to parliamentary democracy, Marxism and Jews. He ruled Germany as a one-party dictatorship under the leader principle, directed the economy toward rearmament and autarky, and presided over the Holocaust.

notes: Answers draw on Mein Kampf, the 25-point programme and the regime's laws and acts. Where the programme and the record differ (point 13 nationalisation versus privatisation; Mein Kampf's praise of unions versus their abolition in 1933; point 17 land reform), the record in power is used, at lower confidence where the two conflict. Historical-figure inferences are marked 'Inferred:' and kept at low confidence. The 1941 decree on homosexuality and Hitler's role in the Holocaust are as described by USHMM and Wikipedia; Hitler did not leave a written order for the genocide. Later pass 2026-11-13 (rules 7): sources tagged by kind. Answers that rested only on Wikipedia pages are re-sourced to primary texts read this pass (the GHDI collection of Nazi-era laws, decrees, speeches and memoranda; USHMM) or nulled with review history. Texts read: Enabling Act, Reichstag Fire Decree, laws on parties, party-state unity, the Hitler Youth, hereditary farms, police chief decree, Concordat, 1941 SS decree, Hossbach protocol, speeches of 1933-1941, the 1936 autarky memorandum, and Mein Kampf (full text, local copy).
